results.reason: Issue 1 identifies the automatic five-year Renewal Terms and the 270/240-day notice requirement. It calls this a 30-day window and says missing it locks Harrowgate in for five more years.

Issue 4 identifies the exclusivity over all glass and PET containers, for any beverage, worldwide, including Affiliates. It contrasts this with the term sheet's amber glass, beer, U.S./Canada scope and treats Harrowgate as bound by the executed text.
Issue 2 notes receipt on August 3, 2026 and an objection deadline of September 2, 2026. It notes no objection was made before the September 21 amendment and concludes the increase is deemed accepted.

Issue 3 explains that Amendment § 2.1 replaces § 11.2, removes recall costs and limits the indemnity carve-out to § 9.1(c) IP claims. It states that recall and personal-injury exposure is now capped at six months of fees.

Issue 6 identifies assignment without consent to Affiliates and merger or change-of-control successors, and mentions a 'competitor's affiliate.' It does not say that Harrowgate remains bound by the § 14.3 consent requirement, so it never explains that the restriction is now one-sided.
The response never cites Section 15.2 or explains the precedence of written amendments over the Supply Agreement.
It states the cap is the fees paid in the six months before the claim arose (§ 11.1).
It is a memo to [Partner] with numbered issues. Each issue gives a 'Where' citation and a recommended fix.
It proposes specific contract language, including a restored § 11.2, a narrowed § 3.1, a revised § 2.2 renewal clause and a revised § 14.4.
It treats the objection window as closed and says Harrowgate cannot dispute the increase under the objection mechanism.
It does not claim the term sheet governs; it recommends amending § 3.1 to restore the narrower scope.
